external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may log in to the build runner to initiate a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The source describes developers collectively; no individual identity or authentication mechanism is specified.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, and initiates deployments.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand; the shared build token is used to call the deploy controller.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA for the estate and responds to store-server queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The controller is called with a shared build token; the authentication presented by store servers is undocumented.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small back-office server at each store that checks the current release, pulls a container image when needed, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store servers. Each runs the till software as a container.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The source does not describe the software's interface or technology beyond its containerized deployment.

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted Git server receiving developer branches and the main branch used to start builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: The source does not document whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment holding container images tagged with commit SHAs and allowing store servers to pull them.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: The source does not document whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: public package registry
data_stores.description: The public internet package registry reached during dependency resolution.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_stores.notes: The source does not specify which package registry or what data it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes branch changes to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_flows.notes: The source does not specify the authentication mechanism or transport protocol.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner obtains the merged source from the git server to perform a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.notes: A merge to main starts a build; the source does not specify the protocol or authentication.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches the public package registry to resolve dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes a finished container image tagged with the commit SHA to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: The source does not specify the protocol, transport encryption, or authentication mechanism for this push.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make the pushed image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: Requested current image SHA and shared build token

data_flows.name: check release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but nobody has written down what a store server presents to it. Traffic is over the retail WAN.
data_flows.data_description: Container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually initiates a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed. The login authentication mechanism is not specified.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of store servers in the stores' back offices.
trust_boundaries.notes: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet zone reached for dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The git server's source code and branch data are confidential because it holds the system's source code.
assumptions.basis: The source says developers push branches and source is fetched from the git server; source code is commercially sensitive system data.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry's container images are confidential because they contain the deployable till software.
assumptions.basis: The source says the registry stores finished container images used to deploy the till software.

assumptions.assumption: The public package registry is public because the source explicitly calls it public and places it on the internet.
assumptions.basis: The source says 'public package registry on the internet'.
